sources.title: Jonathan Ho, Ajay Jain, and Pieter Abbeel, Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (2020), arXiv:2006.11239

author_read_locators.locator: §2 Background and Eqs. (1)–(7), PDF pp. 2–3; §3.2–§3.4 and Algorithm 1, PDF pp. 3–5; Appendix A Eqs. (17)–(22), PDF pp. 13–14.
author_read_locators.disposition: The paper supplies the forward/reverse model conventions, closed marginal, conditioned posterior, endpoint and per-step ELBO terms, epsilon parameterization, weighted KL loss, simple unweighted objective, and telescoping derivation. The local theorem supplies the complete hypotheses and proof. The paper's discretized decoder for quantized image data is out of scope; the assigned model uses a positive-variance Gaussian likelihood on Euclidean data. Section 4 sample-quality, FID, likelihood-comparison, and progressive-coding claims are not imported.

sources.title: Simon J. D. Prince, Understanding Deep Learning, Chapter 18: Diffusion models (2026), pp. 363–387; full online chapter transcription

author_read_locators.locator: Chapter 18, “The diffusion kernel and the marginals,” “The reverse process and the tractable conditional,” “The diffusion ELBO,” and “Simplifying it”; full chapter pages 363–387, online text lines 204–221, 269–288, and 313–333.
author_read_locators.disposition: The chapter independently derives the Gaussian marginal, distinguishes the generally non-Gaussian unconditional reverse law from the tractable posterior conditioned on x0, and reduces the denoising KL to squared mean/noise error. Its terminal-prior cancellation is explicitly approximate for large noise; this batch retains the exact finite-T prior KL. Its implementation and empirical sample-quality claims are not imported.
